items.author: BRamseyKSR
items.text:
Part of what is so frustrating about Kentucky defensively is there is no clear pattern to the game plan or execution. It is hard to even evaluate because it is hard to establish what they are TRYING to do.

Clip 1: Why is Zoom Diallo helping? To the extent that help at the rim is needed Malachi Moreno is there. Gives up an easy, inside-out 3.

Clip 2: Milan Momcilovic gets put on skates and Ousmane N'Diaye helps off of a 40% shooter who has attempted four 2's all year.

Clip 3: Right, wrong, or otherwise the first two clips would make you think Kentucky's game plan or goal is to REALLY be aggressive in the gaps and protect the rim at all costs. However, then how do you explain Milan Momcilovic in this clip? If you sell out on protecting the rim at all costs in the first two clips why isn't he all of the way in at the mid line tagging the roll? 

These "mistakes" don't even fit together.

items.author: BRamseyKSR
items.text:
The defensive miscues late in the first half were plentiful.

Northern Arizona hit four 3's in the final four minutes of the half. Kentucky ended up scoring 45 points...easily SHOULD have led by 14 instead of 8 at the half.

First Clip: Absolutely terrible transition defense. No organization or communication. What is Zoom Diallo doing??? Just watching the ball while #2 Komin gets a wide open 3.

Second Clip: Same thing we talked about with Moreno. #2 Komin has made three 3's at this point...maybe get out there and make him drive it!!!

The OFFENSE gave Kentucky a chance to put this game away in the first half, but the defense in the final four minutes was absolutely awful.

items.author: BRamseyKSR
items.text:
Kentucky's lack of connectivity, focus, and concentration defensively is very frustrating. It cost them a chance to potentially turn Friday's game into a blowout in the first half.

First Clip: 'Cats make a run to go up 10 into a timeout. N'Diaye & Wilkins get hung up on a switch, Wilkins then fouls #22 Bennett on a 3. Not sure who is at fault here, but both of those guys are involved in a LOT of communication breakdowns.

Second Clip: I'm a BIG proponent of switching ballscreens so I have no issue with what goes on throughout this possession. The end result is N'Diaye & Moreno involved in a ballscreen that puts Moreno on #2 Komin. First, you have to be more AGGRESSIVE at the point of the switch (especially when guarding the best player on the floor). Show a high hand and break his rhythm immediately. Moreno plays with his hands down far too much for a 7-footer. Secondly, as a big man (especially with under 10 seconds on the clock), you HAVE to get out and make him drive this. If "length is our strength" then make these guys drive it and finish 2's instead of rhythm 3's.

What happened in between these two clips? Milan Momcilovic nailed two 3's. Had a chance to go up 15+ and potentially start pulling away, but you let them hang around and gain confidence into the half. In the moment it seems inconsequential, but when you end up needing a miracle to even WIN THE GAME you sure wish the defensive discipline late in the first half was better.
